tickets.title: Tasks need a due date
tickets.description: I want to give a task an optional due date when I add or edit it. The list shows the date next to the task, and an open task whose due date has passed is marked overdue.

steps: P1: Remove 'Due dates' from the out-of-scope list (keep priorities and categories out of scope).

P1: Add a new requirement 'Task due date': a task may have an optional calendar due date (date only, no time), set when adding and set, changed or cleared when editing; an invalid date is rejected; the due date is stored on the server and kept after reopening.

P1: Add a new requirement 'Due date display and overdue': the list shows the due date next to a task that has one; an open task whose due date is before today (user's local date) is visibly marked overdue; a done task or a task without a due date is never marked overdue; list order of REQ-007 stays unchanged.
P1: Update REQ-001 and REQ-005 texts and criteria to mention the optional due date on add and edit.
P2: Add optional attribute dueDate (ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD or null) to Task DSN-005.
P2: Extend TaskController DSN-006 create body with dueDate and update body with dueDate (null clears it).
P2: Extend TaskService DSN-007 add and add a setDueDate (or edit) operation with date validation; update SEQ-002 and SEQ-004 accordingly.
P2: Extend TaskStore DSN-008 to persist dueDate (new nullable column with migration of existing databases).
P2: Update UC-001, UC-002, UC-004 descriptions and Browser page DSN-003 for due date input, display and overdue marking; link the new requirements.
P3: Add tests for the new requirements' acceptance criteria and adjust UC-001, UC-002, UC-004 tests.
P4: Implement dueDate in Task, TaskStore (column and migration), TaskService validation, TaskController and app routes, and the date input, display and overdue marker in public/index.html.
P5: Run all tests and check that existing tasks without due date still load and behave as before.

report.text:
The ticket asked for an optional due date on tasks: you can set it when adding or editing a task, the list shows it next to the task, and an open task whose due date has passed is marked overdue.

Requirements (P1): "Due dates" is no longer out of scope. Two requirements were added. REQ-009 covers the optional date-only due date: you can set it on add, and set, change or clear it on edit. It is stored on the server, invalid dates are rejected, and existing tasks without a due date still load. REQ-010 covers showing the due date and marking overdue. Overdue is judged against the user's local date, and the REQ-007 ordering stays the same. REQ-001 and REQ-005 were extended with criteria for adding and editing a due date. The P1 run left a note about REQ-003, but the brief cuts it off, so check it yourself.

Design (P2 and P3): The first design pass gave Task a nullable dueDate and added optional dueDate parameters to the controller and service. The overdue criteria were left to the browser page and had no method covering them. The first review proposed a client-side presenter. The second design pass instead put the rule on the server. TaskService.isOverdue is true only for an open task whose due date is strictly before the given day. GET /api/tasks takes an optional today parameter (the page's local date) and returns TaskView records, a new design element (DSN-009) that adds an overdue flag. TaskService also gained normalizeDueDate. SEQ-001, SEQ-002 and SEQ-004 and the use cases UC-001 to UC-004 were updated to match. The second review proposed a TaskListView class to cover the visual criteria (REQ-002 AC3 and REQ-007 AC1). That class does not appear in the final design, so those two criteria still have no class or method covering them in the design.

Code (P4): All the files follow the design.
- **TaskStore:** stores the due date and adds the column to existing databases, so older rows load with null.
- **TaskService:** validates real calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form and computes the overdue flag.
- **TaskController:** no longer sorts the list itself; it leaves ordering to the service. It accepts a PATCH that changes only the due date.
- **The page:** has a date input on the add form, a second prompt for the due date when editing, and shows the date as "(due …)". It also marks overdue tasks in red.

Tests (P5): The tests for UC-001 to UC-005 were updated to the new signatures. UC-005 was only fixed so it compiles. New tests cover the new criteria of REQ-001, REQ-005, REQ-009 and REQ-010. Typecheck is clean and all 48 tests pass. Three it.todo entries remain; two are manual browser checks (REQ-004 AC1 and REQ-002 AC3).

Points to look at:
- **Overdue with no today parameter:** the server falls back to its own date in UTC, not the user's local date. The page always sends today, but other API callers may see a different overdue flag near midnight.
- **Due-date-only PATCH:** to keep the stored text, it loads the whole task list.
- **PATCH response:** it returns a plain Task without the overdue flag. The page reloads the list after each change, so this does not show on screen.
- **REQ-009 AC4:** tests for it exist in both UC-002 and UC-004.
- **Visual criteria:** REQ-002 AC3 and REQ-007 AC1 are still checked by hand only.

steps.summary: The agent removed "Due dates" from out of scope and added REQ-009 (optional date-only due date, settable on add and edit, stored on the server, invalid dates rejected, existing tasks still load) and REQ-010 (due date display and overdue marking for open tasks, with the REQ-007 ordering unchanged), and it updated REQ-001 and REQ-005 to mention the due date. Both the read and the write of the requirements succeeded, and the agent reports no open questions. Before approving, check that REQ-003 should stay as it is, since the plan lists it as affected but gets no step, and decide whether the design and test items that use UC, SEQ and DSN IDs need a follow-up because they are outside this document.

Phase P2 (design) updated the design for REQ-001, REQ-005, REQ-009 and REQ-010 and saved it, adding a nullable `dueDate` to `Task` with matching optional fields in the controller, service and use cases; one `report_coverage` call failed and was retried successfully. Five acceptance criteria remain uncovered: REQ-002 criterion 3 (done-state appearance) as before, and REQ-010 criteria 3 to 6 (overdue marking), which the browser page computes from `dueDate` and `done` but no class or method currently covers. Decide whether the browser page should get a method or class for the overdue rules, or whether the coverage check should accept use-case-level coverage for these, before approving P2.

The agent read the requirements and design, then submitted two design proposals for phase P3: a `TaskPresenter` with an `isOverdue(task, todayLocal)` rule covering REQ-010 AC3–AC6, and a `renderTask` method covering REQ-002 AC3, plus re-render messages added to SEQ-003. All tool calls succeeded, so there are no failures to chase. Review the proposals against the requirements, paying particular attention to whether `todayLocal` is the right way to handle timezones in the overdue rule, and confirm that SEQ-003 still matches the updated design.

The agent added the server-side overdue rule (`TaskService.isOverdue`), the `overdue` flag on `GET /api/tasks`, and a new `TaskView` type, and updated the design docs to match, so all five REQ-010 overdue criteria are now covered by methods. Two criteria remain uncovered because they are visual and depend on browser CSS the agent has not added yet: REQ-002 criterion 3 (done state styling) and REQ-007 criterion 1 (struck-through done tasks). Before approving, check whether you want PATCH to return the overdue flag as well, since the agent left it out and the page currently reloads the list after unticking, and decide whether the two visual criteria should block P2 or move to a later phase.

The agent read the requirements and design, then submitted two design proposals for the uncovered criteria, with no failed tool calls. It proposed a new `TaskListView` class on the Browser page, with `renderTask` covering REQ-002 AC3 (ticked checkbox and struck-through text) and `renderList` covering REQ-007 AC1, each called from the matching sequence (SEQ-003 and SEQ-001). Check whether those two sequences really need the new class and whether the proposal matches how the Browser page is meant to be structured before you approve this phase.

The agent implemented the new design across the source files (Task, TaskView, TaskStore, TaskService, TaskController, app.ts and public/index.html), and detect_drift and start_app both passed. Before approving, check the typecheck failure: it is still failing in four old tests under test/ (UC-001, UC-002, UC-004, UC-005) because they use the old add, editText and list signatures, and the agent could not write to test/, so someone needs to update those tests before the phase can be considered clean. The developer should also confirm that the new nullable due date and the today parameter on list match what the design intends, since the service and controller behaviour (sorting, overdue rules, and the null-versus-undefined handling in editText) were chosen by the agent.

The agent patched the tests for the changed and added requirement IDs across UC-001 to UC-005, and also fixed UC-005, which was not on its list and had broken typecheck by calling `add` with one argument. Typecheck is now clean and all 48 tests pass, with 3 `it.todo` entries, two of which (REQ-004 AC1 and REQ-002 AC3) are manual checks. Before approving, check that the `it.todo` entries are acceptable, that the UC-005 change was intended, and that REQ-009 AC4 being covered in both UC-002 and UC-004 is the coverage you want.

+## REQ-009 Task due date
+
+functional, must
+
+The system shall let a task have an optional calendar due date (date only, no time), which the user can set when adding a task and set, change or clear when editing it, and shall store it on the server.
+
+Acceptance criteria:
+
+- A task without a due date is valid and can be saved
+- A due date entered when adding a task is saved with the task
+- A due date can be set, changed and cleared when editing a task
+- An invalid date is rejected and the previously stored due date is kept (or none when adding, no task is created)
+- The due date contains no time component
+- The due date is still present after reopening the app, including after the browser's local data is reset
+- Existing tasks without a due date still load and behave as before
+
+## REQ-010 Due date display and overdue
+
+functional, must
+
+The system shall show the due date next to each task that has one and visibly mark an open task as overdue when its due date is before today's date in the user's local time zone.
+
+Acceptance criteria:
+
+- A task with a due date shows that date next to its text
+- A task without a due date shows no date
+- An open task with a due date before today (user's local date) is visibly marked overdue
+- An open task with a due date of today or later is not marked overdue
+- A done task is never marked overdue, even if its due date is past
+- A task without a due date is never marked overdue
+- Unticking a done task whose due date is past marks it overdue
+- The list order defined in REQ-007 is unchanged by due dates
+
 ## Out of scope
 
 - User accounts, login and multi-user support
-- Due dates, priorities and categories
+- Priorities and categories
 - Browser-only storage as the sole persistence
